reason: This passage (Ezekiel 37, the Valley of Dry Bones vision) describes God's sovereign action in reviving Israel through the prophet's proclamation. The narrative focuses entirely on: (1) God commanding the prophet Ezekiel to prophesy to the dry bones, (2) God's direct action in assembling the bones, clothing them with flesh and skin, and breathing spirit into them, and (3) Israel represented as passive recipients acknowledging their spiritual death and despair ('Our bones are dried up and our hope has perished'). There is no depiction of leaders and people collaborating or working together; the entire vision centers on God's unilateral restoration of the nation.
